questions.question:
Which of the following are true of sex linked inhertiance in humans?
A. Males are considered to be hemizygous for genes present on X-chromosome
B. Majority of sex-linked traits are carried on the X-chromosome
C. Genes that are not sex-linked are present in somatic cells and absent in germ cells
D. 1:1 ratio of males and females in humans is a result of meiosis in males
E. The single X-chromosome present in the father is inherited by the son (male-to-male transmission)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
1.  A and B only
2.  B and D only
3.  A, B and C only
4.  B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
A. Males are considered to be hemizygous for genes present on X-chromosome: This is true. As males have only one X-chromosome, they have only one copy of each gene located on the X-chromosome. Therefore, males are hemizygous for X-linked genes. B. Majority of sex-linked traits are carried on the X-chromosome: This is also true. The X-chromosome carries many genes that are involved in sex determination and other traits. Therefore, most sex-linked traits are carried on the X-chromosome. C. Genes that are not sex-linked are present in somatic cells and absent in germ cells: This is not true. Genes that are not sex-linked are present in both somatic cells and germ cells. D. 1:1 ratio of males and females in humans is a result of meiosis in males: This is not true. The 1:1 ratio of males and females in humans is due to the fact that males and females have an equal chance of being born. Meiosis in males does not affect this ratio. E. The single X-chromosome present in the father is inherited by the son (male-to-male transmission): This is not true. The son inherits one X-chromosome from the mother and one Y-chromosome from the father.

questions.question:
Which of the following animals exhibit male heterogamety?
(i) Fruit fly 
(ii) Fowl
(iii) Human
(iv) Honey bee
1. (i) and (iii) 
2. (ii) and (iv)
3. (ii) and (iii) 
4. (i) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Heterogamety is occurrence of two types of gametes in one of the two sexes. In human and fruit fly (Drosophila), make is heterogametic (X & Y-chromosomes) and female is homogametic (two X-chromosomes). Male is homogametic (ZZ) and female is heterogametic (Z & W) in fowl. Honey bee exhibits haplodiploid sex-determination system. Male honeybees are born from the unfertilized eggs by the process known as parthenogenesis whereas female honeybees are born from fertilized egg. Since, unfertilized egg carries only half the number of chromosomes as compared to fertilized egg, male honey bees have half the number of chromosomes (n) as compared to female honey bee (2n).

If the unknown seed parent is heterozygous for seed color (Yy), then not all the offspring in the F2 generation will have green seeds. In the F2 generation, you would expect a phenotypic ratio of 3 yellow (YY or Yy) to 1 green (yy) if you perform a test cross (crossing the F1 individual with a homozygous recessive yy individual).
